source.title: A Mechanistic Perspective and Difficulty Metric for Unlearning
source.authors: Jiali Cheng; Zi-Heng Chen; Chirag Agarwal; Hadi Amiri

record.file_problem: Text is readable despite some flattened table formatting and page-break artifacts; no material missing section is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies variation in unlearning difficulty and circuit structure, but it does not test recovery through fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompts, nor whether those attacks recover more than from a model that never learned the knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning-efficacy and general-knowledge results for CUD-selected easy and hard forget sets. Those results bear on sample-level unlearning difficulty, not the listed recovery versions. The paper's circuit findings are descriptive and do not ablate a direction or test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge. No cited results from other papers are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes CUD, a pre-unlearning metric of per-sample unlearning difficulty. It compares unlearning efficacy on CUD-selected easy and hard TOFU and MovieLens forget sets. It applies no relearning, activation-ablation, quantization or prompting attack. It does not test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge, and proposes no attack-robust method. Eldan & Russinovich (an original source) and Fan et al. 2025 on relearning robustness are only cited in passing. Its efficacy and general-knowledge numbers measure forgetting difficulty across sample sets, not whether forgetting is shallow.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that CUD, computed before unlearning, separates easy and hard samples stably across methods. Easy samples use shallower, early-to-mid MLP circuits; hard samples use deeper, output-proximal pathways.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a circuit-guided difficulty metric and uses existing unlearning methods to evaluate selected forget sets; it does not reproduce or test a recovery-attack recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: CUD-selected easy and hard forget sets change unlearning outcomes. The paper also reports robustness of its metric to similarity measures and unlearning-loss choice, but does not test sensitivity to recovery attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: On TOFU forget10 (Llama-3.2-1B), averaged over four methods, unlearn efficacy is 43.7 on the CUD hard set, 57.8 on the default set and 61.1 on the easy set. General knowledge is 73.1, 75.5 and 75.3 respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-sample unlearning difficulty varies and can be predicted before unlearning from circuit similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLM-recommendation unlearning (GPT2, Llama3), CUD hard sets lower unlearn efficacy by about 20 points and retain by about 16 points. Easy sets raise both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CUD-based difficulty stratification transfers to recommendation unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (venue as stated)
record.problems: The reported unlearning efficacy and general-knowledge metrics do not test recovery attacks or compare attacked unlearned models with models that never saw the knowledge. Some table values are presented with flattened layout in the supplied text; the method, forget-set, and metric associations are supported by the table structure and surrounding text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported Table 1 or Tables 6–7 outcomes omitted. Circuit edge distributions and CUD/MRD/context-length correlations were not recorded as rows because they do not measure the recovery behavior in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No attack is applied, so 'simple attacks don't recover it' is untested. Forget efficacy (1−ROUGE, 43–68) is not shown to reach chance.
Circuits are found on the original model only. Nothing is ablated to restore knowledge, and there is no block-vs-delete analysis of unlearned models.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probes.
No method is proposed or tested for robustness to recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's Retain column (e.g., hard sets average 64.3 vs 66.7 default) and the Table 5 similarity-metric variants are not recorded as rows, despite the rows_left_out statement. They bear on no version, so they are not listed under missing. The record's relation 'discusses' overstates engagement; recovery attacks are never discussed beyond one citation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test targeted knowledge accuracy near chance together with recovery attacks, or whether simple attacks fail while general ability is retained.
No fine-tuning or other relearning attack is applied after unlearning.
No activation direction is ablated to restore knowledge, and the paper does not test whether the unlearning methods block access rather than delete knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context-information recovery test is applied.
No method is tested for resistance to the listed recovery attacks.
